name: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
eligibility: New Americans (immigrants and children of immigrants) age 32 or younger pursuing graduate degrees
why: $90,000 over two years for graduate school. Join a network of 835+ Fellows across 103 countries making significant contributions to US society, culture and academia.

name: Thiel Fellowship
eligibility: Young people age 22 or younger building new ventures
why: $200,000 over two years to skip college and build something new. Access to Peter Thiel's network of founders, investors, and scientists.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge 2026
eligibility: Students ages 13–18 worldwide; submit a 2-minute video explaining a concept in physics, life sciences, or mathematics
why: $250,000 post-secondary scholarship, a $50k teacher prize, and a $100k school lab for the best 2-minute science video. No lab or team required; open now through September 15.

name: YC Summer Fellows Grants
eligibility: Undergraduate CS or engineering students worldwide; no company required
why: $20k cash + $90k in compute credits to build a self-directed AI project in SF. YC picks 20–50 students; no company or team required.

name: Apple AIML Residency 2026
eligibility: Master's/PhD graduates, software engineers, academics seeking industry experience
why: One-year paid residency at Apple working on ML products that impact millions. Residents publish at premier venues like NeurIPS while gaining direct Apple mentor access.

name: Anthropic AI Safety Fellows
eligibility: Engineers and researchers with strong Python background; must have right to work in US, UK, or Canada
why: $3,850/week stipend and $15k/month in compute for full-time AI safety research. 80%+ of past fellows published a paper; 40%+ received a full-time Anthropic offer.

name: Agentic Cinema: The Blockbuster Hackathon
eligibility: Above legal age worldwide; some countries excluded; must build with Gemini and Google Cloud
why: $75,000 across five sponsor tracks (IBM, Grafana, Replit, Clickhouse, Parallel). Build AI agents for media workflows using Gemini and Google Cloud. Submit by September 7.

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
organizer: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy
eligibility: Undergrads through professionals worldwide; DC track requires US work authorization
why: $15–22k stipend, two-week DC residency, direct mentorship from leading AI governance experts. Past fellows joined CSET, GovAI, and major tech policy shops.

name: a16z Speedrun Alpha Fellowship
eligibility: Software engineers and recent grads within 3 years of graduation; US work authorization required; full-time in-person commitment
why: $20k equity-free grant + $250k follow-on on the startup track, or full-time placement at Substack, Sesame AI, and other a16z portfolio companies. Cohort 2 opens September 2026.

name: ETHOnline 2026
eligibility: Open to all builders worldwide; solo or team; small ETH stake required to secure a spot
why: $100,000+ in sponsor prizes across a 10-day async global hackathon. Build from scratch or extend open source — no travel required.

name: AI Alignment Research Fellowship 2026
eligibility: Any career stage with strong ML background and AI safety interest; full-time 40 hrs/week; contractor payment capability required; apply by August 17
why: $12,000 stipend plus cloud compute budget for 8 weeks of full-time AI safety research with AE Studio mentors. Six spots per cohort; demo day with travel covered in Los Angeles.

name: MLH Fellowship Fall 2026
eligibility: Age 18+; coding proficiency in at least one language; 20+ hrs/week commitment; non-embargoed country
why: 12-week remote open source fellowship — contribute to projects used by millions under mentorship from senior engineers at top tech companies. Need-based stipend available.

name: SPAR Research Fellowship Fall 2026
eligibility: Undergraduate, graduate, and PhD students worldwide; technical or policy background preferred; no prior research experience required
why: 3-month mentored AI safety research with project compute covered. Past fellows published at ICML and NeurIPS; cohorts led to job offers at METR, Redwood, GovAI. Apply by August 18.

name: Richard Tapia Celebration of Diversity in Computing
eligibility: Students from underrepresented groups in computing; scholarships available
why: Full scholarships covering travel, hotel, and registration. Career fair access to Google, Microsoft, and Meta engineers that is difficult to replicate any other way.

name: HackMIT 2026
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students from any university worldwide; applications open in August
why: MIT's flagship 24-hour hackathon with 1,000+ college hackers. Sponsor challenges include cash prizes and direct internship and full-time interview pipelines at top tech companies.

name: Hack the North 2026
organizer: Hack the North / University of Waterloo
eligibility: Students at any education level worldwide (13+); travel and accommodation covered for non-Waterloo attendees
why: Canada's largest hackathon. 36 hours, free admission, travel and lodging covered for non-local attendees. Cash sponsor prizes and direct interview pipelines at top tech companies.

name: MHacks 2026
eligibility: Students currently enrolled in or recently left any high school, college, or university worldwide
why: $30,000+ in prizes at one of the world's largest collegiate hackathons. 1,000+ hackers from 100+ universities over 36 hours with strong alumni-to-company placement track record.

name: Recurse Center Fall 2 2026
eligibility: Anyone with solid programming experience; no degree or enrollment required; need-based grants available
why: Tuition-free 12-week programming retreat in Brooklyn (or remote) in a peer cohort of ~30. Integrated recruiting places alumni at Stripe, Google, and top startups. Apply by Sep 3.

name: ETHGlobal Tokyo 2026
eligibility: Open to all builders worldwide
why: Elite Web3 hackathon in Asia's tech capital. Large prize pool, beginner-friendly mentorship, and access to leading blockchain innovators. Refundable ETH stake ensures participant commitment.

name: HackHarvard 2026
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students worldwide; teams up to 4
why: Harvard's 36-hour flagship hackathon. Themes span health, climate, and civic tech. Significant prize pool and industry mentorship; free for all student applicants worldwide.

name: Claude Corps
eligibility: 18+, US work authorization required, under two years full-time work experience; no education requirement; apply by July 17
why: $85k/year salary + benefits to deploy AI at nonprofits nationwide. Anthropic's $150M flagship initiative — 100-fellow first cohort starts October 2026. Apply by July 17.

name: AI Genesis Hackathon 2026
eligibility: Open to all builders worldwide; solo or team; online build phase is global, top teams invited to the Dubai finale
why: $45,500+ across six AI tracks — security, generative AI, Web3, collaboration tools, autonomous agents, and industry solutions. Online build phase is global; top teams earn a trip to the Dubai finale.

name: Grace Hopper Celebration 2026
eligibility: Students and professionals who identify as women or non-binary in tech; scholarships available
why: The world's largest gathering of women in tech (~30,000 attendees). AnitaB.org scholarships cover full attendance. Career fair is a direct path to top company offers.

name: ETHGlobal Mumbai 2026
eligibility: Open to all builders worldwide; solo or team; small ETH stake required
why: 36-hour ETHGlobal hackathon in Mumbai — multiple sponsor prize tracks and on-site mentorship from leading Web3 protocols. Finalist teams demo live to judges.

name: Junction 2026
eligibility: Open to all builders worldwide; limited travel grants for strongest international applicants
why: Europe's largest hackathon — 2,000 builders, 48 hours, €100,000 in prizes. Travel grants for top international applications; apply by September 6.

name: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
eligibility: All ages and skill levels worldwide; solo or team participation at local venues globally
why: The world's largest annual hackathon, run by NASA. Teams use real NASA data to solve space and Earth challenges. 100k+ participants at 150+ local events; global winners earn NASA recognition.

name: Outreachy December 2026
eligibility: People facing underrepresentation or systemic bias in the tech industry of their country; applications open August 2026
why: $7,000 stipend to contribute to major open source projects (Linux, GNOME, Mozilla) for 3 months. Applications open late August; one of the most accessible paid open source programs.

name: NeurIPS 2026
eligibility: Open to all; student travel grants via NeurIPS financial assistance, Citadel, and Jump Trading — deadline October 2026
why: World's premier ML/AI conference — 14,000+ attendees, top researcher talks, and student travel grants from NeurIPS, Citadel, and Jump Trading that cover full attendance costs.

name: Citadel NeurIPS Travel Grant 2026
eligibility: Current bachelor's, master's, or PhD students in CS, math, statistics, or quantitative fields; preference for NeurIPS paper submitters
why: All-expenses-paid trip to NeurIPS — the world's top ML conference. Citadel books flights, hotel, and conference pass. Open to undergrads. Apply by October 5.

name: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
eligibility: Enrolled students 18+ at accredited institutions worldwide; teams of 1–4; free to enter
why: $50k–$100k in cash prizes across two tracks. Scale Track winners meet Satya Nadella and receive Microsoft for Startups support. Registration open now.

name: MATS Winter 2027
eligibility: Anyone 18+ worldwide motivated by AI safety; all backgrounds welcome; no prior publications required
why: $1,600/week stipend plus free housing, meals, and travel for 12 weeks of full-time AI safety research in Berkeley or London. No prior publications required. Apply by Sep 6.
